readings.title: The order that disappeared between shifts
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: At a small distribution office, each employee kept a separate notebook. A customer asked to change a delivery address during the morning shift. The employee wrote it down, but the afternoon team used the original address. The manager did not solve the problem by asking everyone to remember more. Instead, the office created one shared change log linked to order numbers. Whoever accepted a change recorded it immediately. The next shift acknowledged reading it. Personal notebooks remained useful for reminders, but the shared log became the authoritative record of customer requests.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：篇章结构与信息判断

readings.title: A repair team's realistic promise
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A repair company used to promise an exact arrival time for every home visit. Traffic and unexpected faults often made that promise impossible to keep. Customers became frustrated even when repairs were completed well. The company began offering a two-hour arrival window and a message when the technician left the previous job. It also asked customers whether they needed extra notice to return home. Some preferred the old system at first. After several weeks, fewer people complained about waiting without information. The company learned that a realistic promise supported by updates could be more valuable than a precise but unreliable one.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：篇章结构与信息判断

readings.title: One question before buying software
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: The manager of a translation office considered buying a new scheduling system because projects were regularly delayed. Before choosing a product, she asked the team where work actually stopped. Translators said they often waited for clients to clarify unfamiliar terms. The office already had enough scheduling tools; it lacked a clear process for asking questions early. The team added a short clarification stage when a project arrived and assigned one contact person for each client. Delays became less frequent. The manager still planned to improve software later, but now knew which problem any new tool should address.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：篇章结构与信息判断

readings.title: Recognising help that remains unseen
readings.instruction: Read the passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: In a hotel, performance reports once focused on the number of guests each employee checked in. This overlooked the colleague who explained procedures to new staff and helped solve difficult requests. Her own total sometimes looked low because she spent time helping others. The team added a brief weekly discussion about support work. They did not attach a score to every friendly action. Instead, supervisors recorded specific examples that affected the whole team's service. The change reminded staff that individual totals could not describe all useful work. It also made training contributions more visible during development conversations.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：篇章结构与信息判断

translation.stem:
Translate the following passage into Chinese:
A good handover makes unfinished work visible. It tells the next person what has happened, what still needs attention, and whom to contact if a question arises. This information should be easy to find and specific enough to act on. A vague instruction such as 'deal with it soon' may sound urgent, but it does not help a colleague decide what to do first.
knowledgePoints: 英译汉：语义准确与中文表达
translation.explanation: 准确处理三个并列宾语从句及specific enough to act on的含义。
translation.referenceAnswer: 良好的交接能让尚未完成的工作清楚地呈现出来。它告诉接手者已经发生了什么、哪些事情仍需关注，以及出现问题时应该联系谁。这些信息应当便于查找，并且具体到足以据此采取行动。像“尽快处理”这样模糊的指示听起来可能很紧急，却无法帮助同事判断应该先做什么。

criteria.name: 意义完整
criteria.description: 准确传达主要信息、条件和因果，不遗漏关键内容。

criteria.name: 语言准确
criteria.description: 词义、指代、时态及句间关系处理正确。

criteria.name: 表达自然
criteria.description: 中文通顺，符合段落逻辑。

writing.stem: Write 100–150 words in English to your team proposing a clearer handover routine. Describe a current difficulty, suggest information that should be recorded, and explain how the team could introduce the routine.
knowledgePoints: 写作：任务完成、组织与语言
writing.explanation: 提出交接问题、记录字段与试行流程，形成可执行建议。
writing.sampleAnswer:
Dear colleagues,
Recently, several customer changes have reached the next shift too late. Important details sometimes remain in personal notebooks, so another person cannot easily find them.
I suggest a shared handover log for all unfinished requests. Each entry should include the customer or order number, the action already taken, the next step, and the deadline. It should also name the person who can answer questions. At the start of a shift, one team member could confirm that the new entries have been read.
We could try this routine for two weeks and discuss whether any fields are unnecessary or missing. Keeping the log short should make it practical during busy periods. I believe this small change would help us give customers more reliable service.
Best wishes,
A team member
